title: CLEAR Travel Tips: Can You Bring Wedding Gifts on a Plane?
summary: Want to bring a wedding gift on your next flight? Learn how to pack common wedding gifts, when to ship them, and where to check TSA guidance before you travel.
body_markdown:
Traveling to a wedding often means bringing more than just your suitcase, but taking a wedding gift on a flight requires a little extra planning.


The good news is that most wedding gifts can travel on a plane. Whether an item belongs in your carry-on or checked bag, or if it should be shipped separately depends on what you're bringing and whether it's fragile or valuable.


‍


## Can You Bring Wedding Gifts on Your Flight?


In most cases, yes. Wedding gifts are generally permitted through airport security, but they still need to meet TSA screening requirements.


Some gifts may require additional screening, while others are better suited for checked luggage. Before you pack, think beyond whether an item is allowed—consider whether it's fragile, valuable, oversized, or difficult to replace if it's damaged during your trip.


If you're unsure about a specific gift, use the TSA's What Can I Bring?[tool](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/security-screening/whatcanibring/all?viewsreference%5Bcompressed%5D=eJxdkNEKgzAMRf8lz32QbjDwZ0pGYw20VWp0iPjvtivq2ENobu-5CWQDi4LQboDJzYGiQBtn7xX0hJbSqTwHvqyh6ya61IiucAAKhMVT_d8VUMS3J2syKxzdVLaccH3Vz9a73cvMlDuTi2U1so70zSR0Ccce_gG22dbN8zY6Jm9NxFCCVSxMnxtItPDEQ6zZh9b6lc1KslAwlnw5TLMf9GtleQ&page=48) to check whether it belongs in your carry-on or checked bag before you travel.


It's also important to review your airline's baggage policies. Even if a gift is permitted through airport security, it still needs to meet your airline's carry-on size and weight limits. Bulky or unusually shaped gifts may need to be checked, even if they're otherwise allowed in the cabin.


‍


## Should You Wrap Wedding Gifts Before Flying?


If you're traveling with a wedding gift, consider waiting until you arrive to wrap it.


During the screening process, TSA officers may need to inspect wrapped packages. If that happens, the wrapping paper may need to be removed so the item can be screened.


Instead, travel with your gift in a gift bag or pack wrapping paper separately and wrap it once you reach your destination. This helps reduce the chance of damaged wrapping before the festivities.


‍


## Packing Different Types of Wedding Gifts


Not every wedding gift should be packed the same way. Here are a few things to consider before you travel.


### Fragile Gifts


Glassware, crystal, ceramics, artwork, and picture frames deserve extra protection.


Protect fragile items with clothing or packing materials, and consider keeping them with you in your carry-on whenever possible to reduce the chance of damage during your trip.


### Wine and Champagne


A bottle of wine or champagne can make a thoughtful wedding gift, but alcohol is subject to different requirements when packed in your checked bag. Wine isn’t subject to quantity limits, while stronger spirits with more than 24% alcohol are limited to 5 liters per passenger and must be in its original, unopened retail packaging. Before traveling, review the latest TSA guidance and your airline's baggage policies to determine the best way to pack it.


### Kitchen Gifts


Cookware, bakeware, and small kitchen appliances are generally durable enough for travel, although larger items may take up valuable luggage space.


If you're bringing sharp kitchen items, such as a knife set, pack it in your checked bag. Make sure it is securely wrapped to help prevent injuries during baggage handling and inspection. Confirm the latest TSA requirements before packing and choose the appropriate bag for your trip.


### Cash, Gift Cards, and Jewelry


Small, valuable gifts should stay with you throughout your trip. Gift cards, cash, jewelry, and sentimental family keepsakes are generally best carried in your personal item or carry-on rather than checked luggage.


##
When Shipping Your Wedding Gift Makes More Sense


Sometimes the easiest way to travel with a wedding gift is not to travel with it at all. Large appliances, bulky home goods, and other oversized registry items can be difficult to fly with. If a gift takes up significant luggage space or adds considerable weight to your bag, shipping it before your flight may be the more convenient option.


Shipping directly to the couple can be a good option if you're attending a destination wedding, flying internationally, traveling with multiple bags, or bringing a large or fragile gift. Many wedding registries also let you ship gifts directly to the couple's home, eliminating the need to pack them altogether.


If you choose to ship your gift, check with the wedding couple beforehand to make sure it arrives at the right location and at the right time.
